{{Short description|Japanese mathematician (born 1972)}}
[[File:Takuro Mochizuki cropped Takuro Mochizuki 20110412.jpg|thumb|200px|Takurō Mochizuki]]
'''Takurō Mochizuki''' (望月 拓郎, born 28 August 1972) is a Japanese mathematician at [[Kyoto University]].

== Overview ==
As a student at the University of Kyoto in 1994, Mochizuki left his undergraduate studies early to become a graduate student in mathematics at the same university. He completed his Ph.D. in 1999, and joined the faculty of [[Osaka City University]], returning to Kyoto in 2004.<ref name="ku"/>

== Awards ==
[[File:Takuro Mochizuki cropped 1 Takurō Mochizuki.jpg|thumb|200px|Takurō Mochizuki in [[Oberwolfach]], [[Germany]] in 2015]]
He was awarded the [[Japan Academy Prize (academics)|Japan Academy Prize]] in 2011 for his research on [[D-module]]s in [[algebraic analysis]].<ref name="ku">{{citation|url=http://www.kyoto-u.ac.jp/static/en/news_data/h/h1/news7/2011/110412_1.htm|title=Professor Emeritus Masahiro Shogaito and Associate Professor Takuro Mochizuki of the Research Institute for Mathematical Sciences Receive the Japan Academy Prize|date=April 12, 2011|publisher=Kyoto University|accessdate=2015-08-01}}.</ref><ref>{{citation|url=http://www.japan-acad.go.jp/pdf/youshi/101en/mochizuki.pdf|title=Japan Academy Prize to: Takuro Mochizuki|publisher=Japan Academy|accessdate=2015-08-01}}.</ref> In 2014 he was a [[list of International Congresses of Mathematicians Plenary and Invited Speakers|plenary speaker at the International Congress of Mathematicians]].<ref>{{citation|url=http://www.icm2014.org/en/program/scientific/plenary|work=Seoul ICM 2014|title=Schedule of Plenary Lectures|accessdate=2015-08-01|url-status=dead|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20150716122702/http://www.icm2014.org/en/program/scientific/plenary|archivedate=2015-07-16}}.</ref>

Mochizuki was awarded the 2022 [[Breakthrough Prize in Mathematics]] for his work on "the theory of bundles with flat connections over algebraic varieties".<ref>{{cite web|url=https://breakthroughprize.org/News/65|title=Winners of the 2022 Breakthrough Prizes in life sciences, fundamental physics and mathematics announced|access-date=9 September 2020}}</ref> The same year, he became a laureate of the [[Asian Scientist 100]] by the ''[[Asian Scientist]]''.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.asianscientist.com/as100/ |title=The Asian Scientist 100 |author= <!--Not stated--> |date= |website= |publisher= [[Asian Scientist]] |access-date= 13 March 2025 |quote= |language= }}</ref>
